compiled_from: One row per (RxNorm ingredient, effect condition) pair that FDA labeling states outright. A row is written only when each of its four claims has a source this project can re-read: the effect (a span into a hashed SPL), the ICD-10 code (NLM Clinical Tables), the SNOMED codes a chart already carrying the condition would hold (the pinned Synthea jar's own modules), and the structured signal (a LOINC code with a declared threshold). A claim with no such source is declared in the row, never omitted and never supplied from memory (REQ-62, D118).
known_limit: Five rows. Two drugs were dropped rather than written: warfarin, because no section of its label states hypotension, and clopidogrel, because its label states aplastic anemia and pancytopenia -- suggesting anemia, unspecified from a low haemoglobin on a clopidogrel chart would be a different claim than the source makes. One row carries an empty already_coded with its reason. The table is the size the documents make it, not the size the version's plan asked for. The SNOMED provenance names every Synthea module that declares each code, but the jar is 200 MB and gitignored, so that provenance is checkable by hand against the pinned hash and not by any gate -- the gate checks that a source block is present and well formed.

source.origin: RxNav, U.S. National Library of Medicine

effect.quote: Corticosteroids decrease bone formation and increase bone resorption both through their effect on calcium regulation (i.e., decreasing absorption and increasing excretion) and inhibition of osteoblast function. This, together with a decrease in the protein matrix of the bone secondary to an increase in protein catabolism, and reduced sex hormone production, may lead to inhibition of bone growth in pediatric patients and the development of osteoporosis at any age.

signal.rationale: The WHO operational definition of osteoporosis, which is what a DXA report is read against. No document in either corpus states it, so it is a declared constant and not a span (D40, D51). The LOINC code is the one the pinned Synthea jar emits for a T-score.

rows.unsourced_reason: No SNOMED code for hypotension is reachable. The pinned Synthea jar declares none in any of its 111 modules, and no credential-free SNOMED source exists -- browser.ihtsdotools.org and snowstorm.ihtsdotools.org both answer Access Denied, and NLM Clinical Tables carries no SNOMED identifier (D36, re-checked for T-96). The consequence, stated rather than hidden: a chart that already codes hypotension in SNOMED will be suggested it again, and this row's would_affect is empty by construction. Both are false suggestions, never false verdicts.

signal.rationale: The conventional adult threshold for hypotension. Declared, not read from a source: the ELIQUIS label names the effect and quantifies nothing (D40, D51).

rows.note: Spec section 11's anticoagulant example, written against apixaban rather than warfarin. The JANTOVEN warfarin label states no hypotension anywhere in its boxed warning, contraindications, warnings or adverse reactions; its one use of anemia names it as a risk factor for bleeding rather than an effect the drug causes (D118).
